statement: Use the trapezium rule with $4$ strips to estimate $\\int_{0}^{1}e^{-x^{2}}\\,dx$. Give your estimate to $4$ decimal places and comment on whether it is an over- or under-estimate.
solution: Strips of width $h=1/4$. Points $x_{0}=0,x_{1}=0.25,x_{2}=0.5,x_{3}=0.75,x_{4}=1$ with $f(x)=e^{-x^{2}}$: $f_{0}=1$, $f_{1}=e^{-0.0625}\\approx0.9394$, $f_{2}=e^{-0.25}\\approx0.7788$, $f_{3}=e^{-0.5625}\\approx0.5698$, $f_{4}=e^{-1}\\approx0.3679$. Trapezium: $\\frac{h}{2}[f_{0}+2(f_{1}+f_{2}+f_{3})+f_{4}]\\approx0.125[1+2(2.2880)+0.3679]\\approx0.7430$. Since $f$ is convex on $[0,1]$ ($f''<0$? actually $f''=-2e^{-x^{2}}(1-2x^{2})$, mixed) the rule is a reasonable estimate; the true value $\\approx0.7468$, so this is a slight under-estimate.
hints: Compute $f$ at the 5 equally spaced points.
